Here is a comprehensive summary of the **Log4Shell** vulnerability from the NIST National Vulnerability Database:

---

## 🔴 CVE-2021-44228 — Log4Shell

### 📌 Overview
- **CVE ID:** CVE-2021-44228
- **Name (CISA):** Apache Log4j2 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
- **Published:** December 10, 2021
- **Last Modified:** February 20, 2026
- **Status:** Analyzed

---

### 🛑 Severity
| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| **CVSS v3.1 Score** | **10.0 / CRITICAL** (maximum possible) |
| **Attack Vector** | Network |
| **Attack Complexity** | Low |
| **Privileges Required** | None |
| **User Interaction** | None |
| **Scope** | Changed |
| **Confidentiality Impact** | High |
| **Integrity Impact** | High |
| **Availability Impact** | High |
| **CVSS v2 Score** | 9.3 / HIGH |

---

### 📋 Description
Apache Log4j2 versions **2.0-beta9 through 2.15.0** (excluding security releases 2.12.2, 2.12.3, and 2.3.1) contain a critical flaw in their **JNDI (Java Naming and Directory Interface)** features used in configuration, log messages, and parameters. The vulnerability does **not** protect against attacker-controlled LDAP and other JNDI-related endpoints.

An attacker who can **control log messages or log message parameters** can execute **arbitrary remote code** loaded from LDAP servers when message lookup substitution is enabled — requiring zero authentication and zero user interaction.

> ⚠️ Note: This only affects **log4j-core** and does NOT affect log4net, log4cxx, or other Apache Logging Services projects.

---

### 🔧 Weaknesses (CWE)
- **CWE-20** – Improper Input Validation
- **CWE-400** – Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
- **CWE-502** – Deserialization of Untrusted Data
- **CWE-917** – Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement

---

### ✅ Fix / Remediation
| Version | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| **2.15.0** | Behavior disabled by default |
| **2.16.0+** | Functionality completely removed |
| **2.12.2, 2.12.3** | Security backports (Java 7 line) |
| **2.3.1** | Security backport (Java 6 line) |

---

### ⚡ CISA Known Exploited Vulnerability (KEV)
- **Added to KEV:** December 10, 2021 (same day as disclosure — actively exploited immediately)
- **Action Due:** December 24, 2021
- **Required Action:** Apply updates OR remove affected assets from agency networks. Temporary mitigations were only acceptable until updates became available.

---

### 🏢 Notable Affected Vendors
The vulnerability had an extraordinarily wide blast radius, affecting products from dozens of major vendors including:
- **Apache** (Log4j core, versions 2.0-beta9 through pre-fix releases)
- **Cisco** (dozens of products: Webex, Unity Connection, Firepower, DNA Center, SD-WAN vManage, and many more)
- **Siemens** (numerous industrial and enterprise products)
- **Intel** (several tools and platforms)
- **NetApp** (Active IQ Unified Manager, Cloud Insights, etc.)
- **Debian / Fedora Linux** distributions
- **SonicWall, Apple (Xcode), Bentley Systems, Snow Software**, and many others

---

### 🔗 Key Resources
- [Apache Log4j Security Page](https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/security.html)
- [CISA Log4j Affected Software Database](https://github.com/cisagov/log4j-affected-db)
- [CERT/CC Vulnerability Note VU#930724](https://www.kb.cert.org/vuls/id/930724)
- [Cisco Security Advisory](https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-apache-log4j-qRuKNEbd)

---

Log4Shell is widely considered one of the most severe and broadly impactful vulnerabilities ever discovered, given its **perfect CVSS 10.0 score**, trivial exploitability, and the ubiquity of Log4j across enterprise Java applications worldwide.
